title: Nil-immersion comparison for Proj of a conormal presentation
statement:
Let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, pqf-def-locnoeth] with ideal $I$. Let $E$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] with a surjection $E\twoheadrightarrow I/I^2$. Regard modules on $Y$ as $\mathcal O_X$-modules by $i_*$, and use the conormal graded algebra and symmetric algebra of [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra, lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction]. Put
$$A_a=I^a\times_{i_*(I^a/I^{a+1})}i_*\operatorname{Sym}^aE,\quad A=\bigoplus_{a\geq0}A_a,\quad B=\operatorname{Proj}_X A,$$
with multiplication on pairs, using relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj]. For any morphism $v:X'\to X$ with $X'$ Noetherian, set $Y'=X'\times_XY$, $I'=I\mathcal O_{X'}$, $v_Y:Y'\to Y$, and $E'=v_Y^*E$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback]. Use the canonical surjection $E'\twoheadrightarrow I'/I'^2$ and define $A'_a$ and $B'$ by the same formula. The natural graded map $v^*A\to A'$ is surjective in every degree and induces a closed immersion
$$h:B'\hookrightarrow X'\times_X B$$
which is an isomorphism over $X'\setminus Y'$ and induces the canonical isomorphism on the inverse-image closed subschemes $P(E')\cong Y'\times_Y P(E)$. The ideal sheaf of $h$ is locally nilpotent; equivalently $h$ is a nil-immersion. In particular it is a universal homeomorphism. Its pullback identifies the degree-one twisting sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] and their canonical trivializations over $X'\setminus Y'$. These comparisons respect identities and composition of base morphisms.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 2.2.1.5 and proof, pp. 230-231; tautological-line comparison on degree-one homogeneous localizations. Relative Proj base change: Stacks Tag 01O3 (constructions, lemma-relative-proj-base-change).

proof.text: Work locally on $X$ and then on $X'$. Write $R$ for an affine base ring, $J$ for the immersion ideal and $M$ for the module of $E$ over $R/J$. The conormal-algebra statement identifies the degree-$a$ comparison with the map $\operatorname{Sym}^a(M)\to J^a/J^{a+1}$. It is surjective: each element of $J^a$ is a sum of products of $a$ elements of $J$, and each class of a factor in $J/J^2$ lifts locally to $M$; changing a factor by $J^2$ changes the product by $J^{a+1}$. Degree zero is the identity of $R/J$. Thus both projections from the fibre product $C_a=J^a\times_{J^a/J^{a+1}}\operatorname{Sym}^a(M)$ are surjective. These calculations also hold on stalks and therefore for the sheaf projections.

source.place: XVI 2.2.1.3, first two paragraphs of proof, pp. 229-230

proof.text: The sheaf $A_a$ is the kernel of the difference map $I^a\oplus i_*\operatorname{Sym}^a(E)\to i_*(I^a/I^{a+1})$. The ideal powers and conormal pieces are quasi-coherent; the symmetric algebra is quasi-coherent, and its homogeneous summands are so on the affine symmetric-degree models. Closed pushforward, binary direct sum and kernel preserve quasi-coherence by the cited statements. Hence $A_a$ is quasi-coherent. On an affine open the sheaf direct sum $A$ is the sheaf associated to $\bigoplus_a C_a$: localization commutes with this direct sum, because each element has finite degree support and its finitely many denominators have a common multiple. Thus $A$ is a quasi-coherent graded algebra. Multiplication of pairs preserves the fibre-product condition, since both comparison maps multiply classes in the same conormal algebra. The degree-zero identification is $R\xrightarrow{\sim}C_0$, $r\mapsto(r,\bar r)$; associativity, commutativity and the unit law are componentwise. Apply the same argument to $A'$.

The kernel $K_a$ of $C_a\to\operatorname{Sym}^a(M)$ consists exactly of $(z,0)$ with $z\in J^{a+1}$. Since $J$ annihilates the second coordinate, $JC_a\subseteq K_a$. Conversely the first projection $C_a\to J^a$ is onto by step 1; lifting the factors in a finite expression $z=\sum_j u_j z_j$, $u_j\in J$, $z_j\in J^a$, gives $(z,0)=\sum_j u_j(z_j,s_j)\in JC_a$. Therefore $K_a=JC_a$ and
$$A/IA\cong i_*\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}(E)$$
as graded algebras. Over $U=X\setminus Y$ the second and common terms vanish and $I=\mathcal O_U$, so $A|_U=\mathcal O_U[t]$, with the canonical generator $t=(1,0)$ in degree one. The same statements hold for $A'$ and $U'=X'\setminus Y'$.

source.place: XVI 2.2.1.3, proof, equality K_n = I A_n and quotient identification

proof.text: Each $A_a$ is locally of finite type. Indeed, near any point choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}R_g$ which is a standard open of an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ from the Noetherian cover in the definition of a locally Noetherian scheme; $R_g\cong R[x]/(gx-1)$ is of finite type over $R$, hence Noetherian by finite-type permanence. Such neighbourhoods form a basis, and the same choice is made on $X'$ in the later steps. There choose finitely many generators of $I^{a+1}$ and a finite frame for $E$ on $Y$. Degree-$a$ monomials in the frame generate $\operatorname{Sym}^a(E)$. Locally lift these finitely many monomials along the second projection of step 1. Together with the finitely many generators $(z,0)$ of its kernel from step 3, these generate $A_a$: subtract a linear combination of the lifts to leave an element in the kernel. Now let $N_a\subset A_a$ be the image of the multiplication $A_1^{\otimes a}\to A_a$. Its image modulo $I$ is all of $\operatorname{Sym}^a(E)$, and over $U$ it is all of $\mathcal O_U t^a$. At a point of $Y$, the finite module $A_a/N_a$ over the local ring satisfies $A_a/N_a=I(A_a/N_a)$, hence also $A_a/N_a=\mathfrak m(A_a/N_a)$; Nakayama gives zero. Thus $N_a=A_a$ everywhere. In particular $A$ is generated in degree one by the locally finite module $A_1$. This also proves the corresponding assertions for $A'$.

source.place: XVI 2.2.1.3, finite type and degree-one generation

proof.text:
For an affine base map $R\to S$ put $J'=JS$. The base-changed immersion has precisely this ideal by the closed-immersion base-change statement. The map
$$(J/J^2)\otimes_R S\longrightarrow J'/J'^2,\qquad\bar z\otimes s\longmapsto sz\bmod J'^2$$
is well-defined and surjective: $J'$ is generated by images of $J$, and $J^2$ maps into $J'^2$. Tensor right exactness applied to $M\twoheadrightarrow J/J^2$, followed by this map, gives the required surjection $M'=M\otimes_{R/J}(S/J')\twoheadrightarrow J'/J'^2$. Pullback on affine sections is tensor product by the cited statement. Symmetric-algebra base change identifies $\operatorname{Sym}_{S/J'}(M')$ with $(S/J')\otimes_{R/J}\operatorname{Sym}_{R/J}(M)$, preserving each degree, since its defining generator map preserves degree and so does its inverse. The map $S\otimes_R C_a\to C'_a$ sends $s\otimes(z,m)$ to $(sz,s\bar m)$ in these identifications. Balancedness and the fibre-product relation follow by applying the same map to $\bar z=\psi(m)$; products, degree and unit are preserved. The formulas commute with restrictions and therefore define $v^*A\to A'$.

source.place: XVI 2.2.1.5, first paragraph; construction of p* A -> A prime

proof.text:
Write $D_a=S\otimes_R C_a$. Reduction modulo $J'$ gives
$$D_a/J'D_a\cong(S/J')\otimes_{R/J}(C_a/JC_a)\cong\operatorname{Sym}^a_{S/J'}(M')\cong C'_a/J'C'_a.$$
The first identification sends $\overline{s\otimes c}$ to $\bar s\otimes\bar c$; its inverse sends $\bar s\otimes\bar c$ to $\overline{s\otimes c}$. The balanced relations and the killed $J'$ and $J$ make both maps well-defined. The middle identification uses step 3 and symmetric-algebra base change. Under these identifications the map of step 5 is the identity. Over $U'$ it is also the identity on $\mathcal O_{U'}t^a$. Its cokernel $Q_a$ is finite, since $C'_a$ is finite by step 4. At a point of $Y'$ right exactness gives $Q_a/J'Q_a=0$, and Nakayama over the local ring gives $Q_a=0$. Outside $Y'$ the cokernel is already zero. Thus $v^*A_a\to A'_a$ is surjective for every $a$, without any flatness hypothesis.

source.place: XVI 2.2.1.5, Nakayama argument for each graded piece

proof.text:
Apply arbitrary relative-Proj base change to the quasi-coherent graded algebra $A$. It identifies $T:=X'\times_X B$ with $\operatorname{Proj}_{X'}(v^*A)$. By surjective graded functoriality, step 6 induces a closed immersion $h:\operatorname{Proj}_{X'}A'\hookrightarrow T$. Over $U'$ both graded algebras are $\mathcal O_{U'}[t]$ and the map fixes $t$, so $h$ is the identity there. The isomorphism $\operatorname{Proj}\mathcal O[t]\cong U'$ is explicit: its sole chart $D_+(t)$ has degree-zero ring $\mathcal O$, and covers. Over $Y'$ the map is the identity on the symmetric algebra by step 6. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}S$ of $X'$ the pullback of $A'$ to $Y'$ has sections $C'\otimes_S S/J'=C'/J'C'\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{S/J'}(M')$ by the affine-sections statement for module pullback and step 3, compatibly with restrictions; so $A'$ pulls back to $\operatorname{Sym}(E')$, and likewise $A$ pulls back to $\operatorname{Sym}(E)$ on $Y$. Applying arbitrary relative-Proj base change again gives
$$B'\times_{X'}Y'\cong\operatorname{Proj}_{Y'}\operatorname{Sym}(E')=P(E')\cong Y'\times_Y P(E)\cong T\times_{X'}Y'.$$
These are the canonical comparisons, since the graded maps on scalars and on the generators of $E$ are exactly those of step 5.

Every point of $T$ lies either over $U'$ or over $Y'$. In the latter case its residue-field morphism to $X'$ kills $I'$ and hence factors through $Y'$; thus it is a point of $T\times_{X'}Y'$. Step 7 is an isomorphism on each of these inverse images. Consequently the closed immersion $h$ is surjective on underlying points. On an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}H$ of $T$, write its inverse image as $\operatorname{Spec}(H/L)$. Then $V(L)=\operatorname{Spec}H$, and the radical/zero-locus statement gives $L\subseteq\sqrt{0}$. This proves that the ideal of $h$ consists locally of nilpotent elements; the next step proves the locally uniform nilpotence required in the statement.

source.place: XVI 2.2.1.5, last paragraph; expansion of the assertion on reduced schemes

proof.text: Choose an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}S$ in $X'$ over an affine open of $X$, with $S$ Noetherian as arranged in step 4 (such opens cover $X'$), and finitely many generators $f_1,\ldots,f_q$ of $(v^*A)_1$ there; these exist by step 4 and tensoring their generators. The degree-one generation of step 4 survives tensor product, so their standard opens cover $T$ over this affine base. On $D_+(f_i)$ the coordinate ring is the degree-zero localization $H=(S\otimes_R C)_{(f_i),0}$. It is generated over $S$ by the finitely many fractions $f_j/f_i$: a numerator of degree $n$ is a sum of degree-$n$ monomials in the $f_j$, and division by $f_i^n$ expresses its fraction as a polynomial in these ratios. Hence $H$ is Noetherian by finite-type algebra permanence. Its immersion ideal $L$ from step 8 is finitely generated by the definition of Noetherian. Since $L\subseteq\sqrt0$, the finite-generated-ideal radical-power statement with zero ideal gives $L^N=0$ for some $N\ge1$. These charts cover, so the ideal sheaf of $h$ is locally nilpotent, as claimed. The case of no degree-one generators gives empty Proj and needs no chart.

source.place: XVI 2.2.1.5, last paragraph, with the Noetherian nilpotence bound made explicit

proof.text: For any morphism $T_1\to T$, base change of $h$ is a closed immersion by the closed-immersion base-change statement. On affine opens over a chart $\operatorname{Spec}H$ of step 9 its defining ideal is $LH_1$, and $(LH_1)^N=L^NH_1=0$. Every prime of $H_1$ contains this ideal, since a nilpotent element maps to zero in the integral domain $H_1/\mathfrak p$. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}(H_1/LH_1)\to\operatorname{Spec}H_1$ is a homeomorphism: primes correspond to all primes of $H_1$, and closed subsets correspond under the same quotient map. These homeomorphisms cover $T_1$. The definition of universal homeomorphism therefore applies to $h$.

source.place: XVI 2.2.1.5, nil-immersion conclusion; affine quotient argument

proof.text: On a degree-one chart $D_+(f)$ of any of the graded algebras in steps 4-9, the definition of the twist identifies $\mathcal O(1)$ with the degree-one localization module. Multiplication by the unit $f$ gives its explicit basis: $H\xrightarrow{\sim}(C_f)_1$, $u\mapsto uf$, with inverse $z\mapsto z/f$. If a fraction $a/f^m$ has degree one, its coordinate is $a/f^{m+1}$ of degree zero. For the map $D=v^*A\to A'$ the induced map of these free rank-one chart modules sends the basis $f$ to the basis $\bar f$; since the pullback of a quasi-coherent module to the affine chart $D_+(\bar f)=h^{-1}D_+(f)$ is the tensor product $(D_f)_1\otimes_H H'$, with $H=D_{(f),0}$ and $H'=A'_{(\bar f),0}$, by the affine-sections statement for module pullback, its pullback is an isomorphism. For scalar extension from $A$ to $v^*A$ the same argument sends $f$ to $1\otimes f$ and gives the corresponding isomorphism under relative-Proj base change. The two comparisons compose to $h^*\mathrm{pr}_B^*\mathcal O_B(1)\cong\mathcal O_{B'}(1)$. On overlaps the bases satisfy $f=(f/g)g$; applying the graded ring map sends this exact relation to its target relation, so the isomorphisms agree and glue. Over $U$ and $U'$ the canonical bases are respectively $t=(1,0)$ and $t'=(1,0)$, and step 5 sends $t$ to $t'$. This proves preservation of the canonical trivializations as well.

source.place: XVI 2.2.1.3-2.2.1.5, tautological-line comparison; Stacks 01N1, lemma-surjective-graded-rings-generated-degree-1-map-proj, via explicit degree-one charts

proof.text: For the identity base map the formula in step 5 sends $(z,m)$ to $(z,m)$. For successive affine base maps $R\to S\to Q$, the direct map and the composite (using tensor associativity) both send $q\otimes s\otimes(z,m)$ to $(qs z,qs\bar m)$ in the final fibre product. Such tensors generate the source module, so the graded maps agree in every degree. These equalities persist on degree-zero chart fractions $a/f^n$, whose image is always the image numerator divided by the $n$th power of the image denominator. They therefore give the identity and composition equalities for the induced Proj morphisms under the canonical fibre-product identifications. On the twisting sheaves the chart basis is always sent to its image basis, so the same equalities hold for their identifications and for $t$ on the complement. All formulas commute with restrictions, completing the identity and composition assertions globally.

source.place: XVI 2.2.1.5, canonical construction; tensor and homogeneous-fraction formulas
